correctness.rationale: Define b_16(n) by f_16/f_1, reduce to f_1^15 over F_2 and use Jacobi cube to count T_i+4T_j mod 2. For M=8n+5 every signed ordered x²+y² solution corresponds eight-to-one to a unique positive triangular pair, giving b_16(n)≡r_2(M)/8 mod2. The classical two-squares formula forces the unique odd exponent ≡1 mod4 of a prime 5 mod8. For the count, terms p^(4a+1) with a≥1 are O(sqrt Y), coprimality correction is O(sqrt Y logY). Split u at Y^.1 and apply the fixed-modulus PNT with an exponential uniform error, then expand Li(Y/u²) using convergent odd-u logarithmic moments. This proves the all-orders coefficients and uniform fixed-J remainders. Saved checker exact partition/triangle/prime parity agrees for n=0..5000; r_2=8 pairs for n=0..400. Finite checks supplement but never substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: Quantifies the precise rarity of odd 16-regular partition values, a natural number-theoretic invariant singled out by existing density and congruence literature. The positive π²/4 leading constant, complete logarithmic coefficient hierarchy, and unique-prime squarefree-kernel criterion jointly reveal cancellation structure unavailable from lacunarity alone. It is meaningful even without an extension to all even regularities: it resolves the sharp growth and lower-order rate of a canonical parity-support census. The result is not claimed to improve a known asymptotic, only to supply this previously absent quantified conclusion within inspected literature.
